selection.rule: Dependency-complete first 24 questions from the question-sheet selection order.

questions.question: What did the traveller believe was the real purpose of human life and living in this world?
questions.answer: He believed the goal of life and its true core is faith.

questions.question: What does the traveller call the Qur'an in terms of its place among books?
questions.answer: He sees it as the most famous, brightest, and wisest book in the world.

questions.question: What claim about the Qur'an makes it especially worthy of examination?
questions.answer: It is said to be unmatched in fame, brilliance, and wisdom, and to challenge rejecters in every age.

questions.question: What does the passage say the Qur'an does to those who reject it in every age?
questions.answer: It confronts them with a standing challenge.

questions.question: Why does the traveller begin with the Risale-i Nur instead of somewhere else?
questions.answer: Because he lives in the current age and sees it as a present witness to the Qur'an’s truth.

questions.question: How does the passage portray the Risale-i Nur’s connection to the Qur'an?
questions.answer: As a work built from the Qur'an’s light and meanings.

questions.question: Which two parts of the Risale-i Nur are said to show many dimensions of the Qur'an’s miraculous character?
questions.answer: The Twenty-Fifth Word and the ending of the Nineteenth Letter.

questions.question: How does the passage present the effect of the strongest proofs found in the Risale-i Nur?
questions.answer: It presents them as so convincing that people who examine them carefully move from criticism to admiration.

questions.question: How are the major arguments in certain parts of the Risale-i Nur characterized?
questions.answer: They are characterized as proving many features of the Qur'an’s miraculous quality in a strong and compelling way.

questions.question: What is a strong one-sentence takeaway from the whole passage?
questions.answer: The passage teaches that a careful seeker should first verify the divine origin of the Qur'an, and that the Risale-i Nur offers powerful support for doing so.

questions.question: How is the traveller’s attitude toward truth described at the beginning of the passage?
questions.answer: He is shown as deeply determined, never satisfied with shallow answers, and eager to keep searching.

questions.question: Why does he want to examine the Qur'an?
questions.answer: He wants to see what it says because it is claimed to be the speech of the One he is seeking.

questions.question: What does the traveller assume about the Qur'an before fully testing it?
questions.answer: He considers the claim that it may be the speech of the Being he seeks, but he still wants proof.

questions.question: What question must be answered before its message can be fully trusted?
questions.answer: Whether it truly comes from the Creator.

questions.question: What made the Risale-i Nur the first place he looked?
questions.answer: His being in the present age made him turn first to a work active and available in that same age.

questions.question: What conclusion does the traveller draw from the fact that the Risale-i Nur cannot be defeated?
questions.answer: He concludes that its true source and authority must be the Qur'an, and that the Qur'an is heavenly speech, not human speech.

questions.question: What is meant by saying the Qur'an is the “sun” of the Risale-i Nur?
questions.answer: It means the Qur'an is the main source of its light, truth, and power.

questions.question: What does that result indicate about the Qur'an?
questions.answer: It indicates that the Qur'an is its true foundation and that it is divine speech rather than a human product.

questions.question: Give a short summary of the passage’s message.
questions.answer: The traveller investigates whether the Qur'an is from Allah, and he finds strong support in the unmatched strength and explanations of the Risale-i Nur.

questions.question: Who does the traveller speak to when beginning his reflection in this passage?
questions.answer: He speaks to his own heart.

questions.question: According to the passage, what is the essence of life?
questions.answer: Faith.

questions.question: How is the Qur'an presented at the start of the passage?
questions.answer: It is presented as a uniquely famous, wise, and radiant book that calls its rejecters to answer its challenge.

questions.question: What result of that struggle is emphasized?
questions.answer: The passage emphasizes that no one can defeat it.

questions.question: What struggle of the Risale-i Nur is mentioned?
questions.answer: Its effort to spread the truths of the Qur'an in an age marked by denial and resistance.
